What is the SFI token used for?

SFI is the governance token of the Saffron protocol. Holders can vote on protocol upgrades, parameter changes, and new pool additions. SFI is bought back on the market using protocol revenue earned by the vault system.
What risks should I be aware of when using Saffron Finance?

As with all DeFi protocols, risks include smart contract vulnerabilities, underlying platform risk, and liquidity risk. Saffron mitigates these through multiple third-party audits, bug bounties, and active monitoring by Hypernative. Users can buy additional deposit coverage on Nexus Mutual.
What are the different tranches on Saffron and how do they affect risk and yield?

Saffron offers senior and junior tranches. Senior tranche liquidity providers receive a fixed, lower-risk yield. Junior tranche providers take on more risk in exchange for higher potential returns. This system lets users self-select their preferred risk/reward balance.
What is Saffron Finance and how does it work?

Saffron is a DeFi native yield exchange system built on Uniswap concentrated liquidity pools. Saffron vaults are permissionless, immutable, and non-upgradable smart contracts live on all EVM chains. Uniswap fees are the first underlying yield source built into Saffron vaults.
How do I get started using Saffron Finance?
Connect your wallet at app.saffron.finance, browse available vaults, and deposit into a vault that matches your risk preference. Alternatively, create a vault using the Create Vault page.
